LESSON: CONSERVING WILD ANIMALS (REPELLING WILD ANIMALS FROM FARMS)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Conserving wild animals (repelling wild animals from farms)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Conserving wild animals (repelling wild animals from farms), part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can we repel wild animals to avoid destruction?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Conserving wild animals (repelling wild animals from farms) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner gives objective ideas as they innovate ways of repelling small wild animals.

Communication and collaboration: The learner exhibits teamwork by contributing ideas and actively participating in innovating ways to

repel small wild animals in a group.

Values:
Unity: The learners collaboratively work together to innovate ways of repelling small wild animals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Socio-economic and environmental safety: The learner discusses the importance of wild animals as a source of tourist attraction.

● Environmental Education: The learner ensures no damages to the environment as they scare away the small wild animals.

Link to other subjects:

● Science and Technology: The learner applies the knowledge of characteristics of animals when repelling the small wild animals.

Suggested learning resources:

• Print and non-print material

• Digital devices,

• Dry materials and source of fire to produce smoke,

• Repellents like chilli and other peppers, garlic, lemon peels, orange peels, lavender, vinegar
